defects.justification: The IPv4-mapped IPv6 check recurses on the text after '::ffff:', but WHATWG URL normalises [::ffff:127.0.0.1] to '::ffff:7f00:1', so '7f00:1' fails both checks and is treated as public. http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/ (or ::ffff:a9fe:a9fe for metadata) gets past the SSRF guard on title fetch.

The DNS check runs separately from fetch(), which resolves the name again, so DNS rebinding (public answer first, internal answer second) reaches internal hosts. The README admits this; the connection should be pinned to the checked IP.

Rethrowing a non-constraint DB error inside an async Express 4 handler gives an unhandled promise rejection, not a call to the error middleware. The request hangs, and on Node >=15 the process crashes.

Every test replaces fetchPageTitle with a stub, so the SSRF guard (private-IP blocking, redirect re-checks, size/timeout limits) that the README advertises has no tests. That is how the ::ffff bypass went unnoticed.
